learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the importance of safety rules, injury prevention in sports, first-aid measures, and how to create a secure environment on and off the field!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Sports injuries are categorized into soft tissue injuries (abrasions, contusions, sprains, strains) and hard tissue injuries (bone fractures and joint dislocations).

The standard first-aid protocol for acute soft-tissue injuries: Protection (prevent further harm), Rest (stop playing), Ice (apply cold pack to reduce swelling), Compression (wrap bandage), and Elevation (raise the injured area above heart level).

Most sports injuries are preventable through proper warm-up and cool-down routines, wearing certified protective gear (helmets, shin guards), ensuring safe playing surfaces, and maintaining adequate hydration.
The immediate, temporary care given to an injured athlete before professional medical help arrives. Its primary goals are to preserve life, prevent the condition from worsening, and promote recovery.

fun_activity.title: 🧊 The P.R.I.C.E. Drill
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine a teammate twisted their ankle during a match. Walk through the P.R.I.C.E. steps: how would you Protect it, why do you apply Ice instead of heat immediately, and how does Elevation help reduce swelling?

exam_tips: 📌 Always clearly differentiate between a 'Sprain' (ligament injury around a joint) and a 'Strain' (muscle or tendon pull).
📌 Memorize what each letter in the P.R.I.C.E. (or R.I.C.E.) acronym stands for—it is a guaranteed exam question.
📌 Explain why proper warm-up and cool-down are the most effective ways to prevent sports injuries.
quick_recap: ⭐ Soft-tissue injuries like abrasions, contusions, sprains, and strains are the most common in sports.
⭐ Never apply heat or massage to an acute soft-tissue injury within the first 48 hours as it increases swelling.
⭐ Safety in sports involves both personal protective equipment and safe environmental conditions.
